messages:
elaine: quick follow-up from the RFC review: we still need to pick how fine-grained deploy controls are exposed. do we: 1) keep everything tenant-level, 2) add per-deployment opt-in endpoints, or 3) introduce a single unified config with explicit scope field? short takes?

mike: single unified config with scope felt clean to me: you pass {scope: "tenant"|"deployment"} on write. router/runtime then resolves. reduces endpoint surface.

ravi: I like the idea but worried about discoverability and accidental cross-tenant writes. We must gate deployment-scoped writes with an explicit permission (eg. "deploy:admin"). Also needs audit entries.

alexa: For Hosted customers, avoid deployment-scoped writes entirely unless they enroll. Most hosted users don't want extra complexity. Dedicated/Private get the opt-in.

elaine: proposal: keep GET/POST /v1/config as tenant-scoped by default. Allow an extra header X-Scope: deployment and path /v1/config?deploy_id=... for deployment-scoped changes. The header plus deploy_id parameter required. This reduces new endpoints but is explicit.

mike: OK but runtime has to be able to differentiate in fast-path codepaths. We can't pay latency to parse optional query params on hot paths. Suggest router normalizes request into context {scope, deploy_id} early.

ravi: caching implications: if we let deploy scope change routing behavior, we must namespace caches. Suggest: cache key = base_key + (scope==deployment ? ":deploy:" + deploy_id : ""). Keep it optional so we don't explode key space for tenant-only customers.

alexa: tracing/telemetry: emit a top-level tag scope=deployment/tenant and deploy.id when applicable. We should also surface which policy produced the final routing decision (policy=deploy_override|tenant_default|system_default) for easier debugging.

ops-bot: ops-bot: FYI - new trace tag `policy` added to dev traces when enabled.

elaine: security: any deployment-scoped write must have a short-lived MFA token if the tenant is hosted (to prevent accidental pinning). Dedicated/Private customers get a service role + audit logs. Thoughts?

mike: MFA for hosted seems heavy — maybe require a secondary confirmation via Console only for hosted tenants. API can return 409 "confirm via console" for sensitive ops. Better UX.

ravi: rollout plan: 1) admin-only console button that creates the deploy-scoped config (debuggable), 2) API locked behind "advanced_deploy" org flag, 3) enable runtime cache split behind flag, 4) 4-week Dedicated canary.

alexa: billing tag: if a deployment sets a model greater than tenant default, we must attach billing.owner=deploy_id+tenant to each token charge. Router will propagate billing tags. Confirm with billing.

elaine: action items: mike - create router normalization patch (add scope/deploy_id to request context). ravi - doc cache key format and perf estimate. alexa - trace tag + policy mapping. I'll draft the RFC appendix for the console flow and the hosted confirmation UX.

mike: I'll spike the router change and post logs. small snippet for normalization I'll add to RFC: 
```
func normalizeRequest(req) {
  ctx.scope = req.header.get('X-Scope') || 'tenant'
  ctx.deploy_id = req.query.get('deploy_id')
  // validate deploy_id permissions early
}
```

ravi: also add note: if deploy_id present but scope==tenant, treat as no-op (ignore). Avoid surprising behavior.

elaine: ok, thanks all. i'll circulate the RFC draft by EOD. keep comments inline on the doc. :white_check_mark:
